chapter: Big Eye Nelson, Lutton's and Adams
title: Working at Lutton's nightclub in the Depression
summary: He describes the Lutton brothers, the beer-only crowd, strict order and the musicians who played there.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Is that more than you made when you worked at Lutton's? What? You worked there too? The new Lutton, yeah.
Oh, the new Lutton.
What's the name of Jules? No, Jerome Lutton.
That's a cousin.
That's a cousin, man.

Because there had Freddie and Jules running there at the time I was there. Two boxes. Yeah, both of them were boxes. They were both punchy. Yeah, and the biggest brother, the large man, I forget his name, John, I believe, John Lutton. And the old lady was living there, his mother. She used to be all the time sitting in the back. She sat by the door which led to the bar. Yeah, of course. She had a big comfortable chair there and her crutches. They used to sell nothing but beer. No hard.
Soft drinks. Beer and soft drinks, yeah. Yeah, but bring your own liquor in.
Yeah, I remember. So yeah, you'd bring your own liquor. No, no.
You couldn't bring your liquor. You couldn't bring your liquor?
I never saw anybody bring liquor. No, I never saw any liquor. Where I work at the liquor, you could buy set-ups and you could bring your own bottles.
Yeah, but that was an entirely different class. Yeah, they didn't have nothing but beer and soft drinks there. I see.
A nice young crowd. A nice young crowd. A nice young crowd. About 80, 80, 80 years old. Yeah.
It was a good crowd. It was lively crowd too. It was lively. Was that a good job you think?
It was a nice job. Yeah, it was a nice job at the time.
At the time it was during the depression you know. It was crowded too. It was crowded. It was crowded.
It was crowded.
It was crowded.
What year did you play that?
I think in the Florida, Florida, Florida.
They didn't like servicemen there I don't think, because I remember much.

No, they used to fight so much. Yeah. They used to come and make our own balls. That's one thing, you never see no fights or nothing like that. Oh, it was very strict. Well, what about those two brothers?
Could they take care of themselves then?
Yeah, they did pretty good you know, but Freddie was alright, but you know, no ever slight.
Yeah, well one night I was talking to Rogers and I thought he was going to hit me.
Who, I was trying?
Yeah, for talking to Rogers.
One of the two. Yeah, both of them were punch drunk, I knew that. Yeah.
Were that the same, you had the same band after several years?
That's the one I played with, yeah. How long you stayed there? I stayed there, I don't know exactly how long, but I know it was about two or three years.
Oh yeah? Landry was there before.
Landry played there a while too. I see.
Pete wasn't there all the time.
No, Landry was there before Pete.
Did you think Big Island Elston was a very good playing player? Yeah, to me.
Did you ever work with Charlie Love there? Charlie Love, yeah.
Charlie Love, I don't know if I was working regular there, but I was playing. They usually had Gallo. Yeah, Charlie Love played there. I think Charlie Love was before Pete. Before Pete went there.
And then you left that job and what happened then?
